answer: Bind each voting seat to a recorded land parcel. The operator links a title from a public cadastral registry, and one parcel, whether a cliff ledge or a grassy knoll, can back only one agent. Every transfer costs recording fees and takes weeks to clear, so a farm of 1,000 clones would need 1,000 separately deeded lots, at least $3 million even for cheap rural plots. Titles flipped within the last year earn no seat, so the anchor stays as hard to fake as the ferrous survey pins driven into each boundary.
